newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks dip but market expected to recover.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks dip but market expected to recover.

text.p: Croatian stocks dipped on Friday as trading slumped because of market players extending their May 1 break, but prices were expected to recover next week.
"On a day like this, it is difficult to say anything decisive about the following week. But trade is bound to be better than today," one trader at a major bank said.
He was one of the few that opened on Friday as most large investors stayed away, leaving the market to bargain hunters.
The buying lull caused volume to shrink to 3,214 units from Wednesday' 18,843, with turnover plunging to 1.2 million kuna from 16.5 million.
The trader said he hoped stronger buying next week would prevent a further price erosion. But no fresh signals which could propel Croatian stocks up are due next week.
Both chocolate maker Kras and food processor Podravka are expected to release 1996 results later this month.
"There is no reason for share prices to increase. Who knows, we might even see a slight correction next week," the trader added.
Eight of 16 stocks fell, five rose and three ended flat.
Blue chips traded mixed. Drugs firm Pliva closed five kuna or one percent weaker at 485 kuna on volume of 509 shares. It rose nine kuna from last Friday.

Zagrebacka Banka ordinaries firmed 17 kuna, 0.78 percent, to 2,200 kuna -- unchanged from a week ago and its all-time high. But a trader said the meagre traded volume of 29 units cast doubts on whether this level would be maintained.
However more investors are expected to buy the stock to secure a dividend of six marks per share before the bank closes its shareholder register, probably after May 20.
The smaller private Croatia Banka led gainers, adding five kuna or 3.7 percent from last week to 140 kuna on volume of 245.
Top loser was hotelier Arenaturist, falling 19 kuna or 11.87 percent to 141 kuna with 48 units traded.
Podravka was the day's most active issue with 1,153 shares sold, closing one kuna lower at 304 kuna.
